transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I've just been having some issues at work lately. We have these really long sales strategy meetings, and... I don't know, I just keep getting up. I know I'm supposed to just stay seated like everyone else, but I always end up getting up to refill my water or... just kind of pace by the printer. So... yeah, that's why I made the appointment.
When you feel that urge to get up and move, what does that feel like in your body or mind?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it. It doesn't really feel like... anything specific, I guess. I just... I just feel like I need to stand up.
When did you first start noticing this difficulty sitting still?

I mean... it's been a while, I guess. Probably... since I switched over to the advertising sales strategy team. That was... maybe a little over two years ago? Like two years and a couple of months. It's just been more noticeable since then, I think.
Thinking back to when you were a child or in elementary school, did you have similar trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, it goes pretty far back. Um... even in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was... bright, but I rushed through things. And... they said I talked out of turn a lot. I also... forgot my homework pretty often, and my desk was always just full of half-finished papers. So... yeah, I guess it's been around for a long time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Presentation (ICD-10 F90.2). Current and historical evidence confirms persistent symptoms in both the inattentive domain (difficulty with organization, task prioritization, chronic disorganization of work materials, childhood history of forgetting homework and leaving tasks unfinished) and the hyperactive-impulsive domain (inability to remain seated during long meetings, restlessness/pacing, childhood history of talking out of turn and rushing). Symptoms have been present since elementary school (prior to age 12) and result in functional impairment at work.
